content:
We have heard the long blast that gathered all Israel, and the single trumpet that called the leaders. Now we come to a third sound, a sharp and urgent alarm. When this alarm sounded the first time, the camp on the east side set out, and tribe by tribe the whole nation began to march. This trumpet is not only about movement. It is about how the New Creation journeys through the wilderness of this world, the narrow way toward the Heavenly Kingdom.

And the beauty of it is that the tribes did not move in a random crowd.

Yahweh arranged them in a set order, and the very names of those tribes carry a spiritual lesson for our own pilgrimage.

When the sharp alarm sounded, the journey began. Our life is not meant to be static. After we have been gathered to Christ and instructed by Christ, we must begin our pilgrimage. We have left spiritual Egypt, but we have not yet entered the fullness of the Kingdom. Between the two lies the wilderness journey, the narrow way. So the alarm trumpet is the call to move forward in obedience, in faith, and in spiritual growth. It is the sound the writer of Hebrews echoes when he urges us, in Hebrews 12:1, *"Let us run with patience the race that is set before us."*

The eastern camp was led by Judah, and Judah means Praise. So, the journey begins with praise. When Yahweh calls us to move forward, we do not begin with fear, complaints, or discouragement. We begin with worship. Just as Paul and Silas sang in the prison at midnight, and just as Jehoshaphat placed singers before the army, the New Creation advances with praise upon its lips. Praise is our way of declaring that Yahweh Himself is leading the journey, and He reminds us in Psalm 50:23, *"Whoso offereth praise glorifieth Me."* Following Judah came Issachar, whose name means Reward or Hire. As we walk the narrow way, we remember that our labour in Christ is never in vain. The road may be hard, but Yahweh has promised an inheritance to those who overcome, for Christ said to the church in Smyrna, in Revelation 2:10, *"Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life."* The pilgrim presses on because we can see the reward ahead. Next came Zebulun, whose name means Dwelling or Habitation. Our hope is not merely to reach a destination but to dwell with Yahweh forever, and every step through the wilderness moves us closer to that eternal home. Paul says this in 2 Corinthians 6:16, *"For ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people."*

When the second alarm sounded, the southern camp moved, led by Reuben, whose name means Behold a Son. As we continue our journey, our eyes remain fixed upon Christ, the Son of God. The narrow way can only be walked by continually looking to Him, which is why we are told, in Hebrews 12:2, *"Looking unto Christ, the author and finisher of our faith."* After Reuben came Simeon, whose name means Hearing. The pilgrim must keep on hearing the voice of the Shepherd, for many other voices compete for our attention, yet the sheep of Christ follow only His. He said plainly, in John 10:27, *"My sheep hear My voice."* Then came Gad, whose name carries the idea of a troop that overcomes in battle. The Christian journey is warfare. There are temptations, trials, persecutions, and spiritual enemies along the road. Yet the saints move forward as overcomers, for Paul declares, in Romans 8:37, *"In all these things we are more than conquerors."*

The western camp was led by Ephraim, whose name means Fruitful.
The purpose of the journey is not only movement but transformation. As we walk with Christ, spiritual fruit begins to appear in us, and Christ tells us why this matters, in John 15:8, *"Herein is My Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit."* Next came Manasseh, whose name means Forgetting. The believer must learn to leave the old life behind, the old failures, the old wounds, the old sins, and the old identities. We move forward by forgetting what is behind, just as Paul wrote, in Philippians 3:13, *"Forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before."* Then came Benjamin, whose name means Son of the Right Hand. Our destination is glory with Christ, for the journey ends where Christ now sits, at the right hand of Yahweh, and the overcomer is promised a share in His victory.

The northern camp moved last and served as the rear guard. It was led by Dan, whose name means Judgment. The believer walks carefully along the way, remembering that Yahweh is righteous and holy. We examine ourselves and live in reverence before Him. With Dan came Asher, whose name means Blessed or Happy. Those who walk with Yahweh are truly blessed, not because the road is easy, but because His presence goes with them every step, as the prophet says, in Jeremiah 17:7, *"Blessed is the man that trusteth in Yahweh."*

Last of all came Naphtali, whose name means My Wrestling or My Struggle. The journey closes with perseverance. The saints wrestle, endure, overcome, and finish their course, and like Jacob, who wrestled through the night, they come out of the struggle carrying a blessing.

See now the beautiful pilgrimage that unfolds when the alarm trumpet sounds. We begin with praise, and look toward our reward, longing for the dwelling place. We keep our eyes on the Son, hearing His voice, and overcoming our enemies. We bear fruit, forget the old life, and reach for heavenly glory.
We walk in reverence, live in blessing, and endure the final struggle until the course is finished. The 12 names reveal our journey.

This is the call of the alarm trumpet. It is the summons for the saints to leave their place of comfort and begin the march through the wilderness, following the cloud of Yahweh step by step, until at last we enter the everlasting Promised Land, which is our eternal home. The trumpet has sounded. The cloud is moving. Let us rise and follow.

title: Prayer
text: Father God, we hear the sound of Your trumpet calling us forward, and we are willing to rise and follow. Teach us to begin every journey with praise, to keep our eyes upon Christ Your Son, and to hear His voice above all others. Make us overcomers in the battle, fruitful along the way, and faithful to the very end. We praise You that Your presence goes with us through every step of this wilderness, and that the cloud is leading us safely home. Bring us at last into Your everlasting Kingdom, our true and eternal dwelling place. In Christ name we pray, Amen.
